model.title: No Antisemitism in Education Act of 2026

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Reported to House):

blocks.text: No Antisemitism in Education Act of 2026

This bill requires local educational agencies (LEAs) and institutions of higher education (IHEs), as a condition of receiving federal funds, to treat discrimination that is motivated by antisemitism as vigorously as the LEA or IHE treats all other forms of discrimination prohibited by Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. (Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits discrimination based on race, color, or national origin in federally funded programs or activities.)

The bill requires federal agencies, LEAs, and IHEs to consider the definition of antisemitism contained in a December 11, 2019, executive order when reviewing or investigating whether a discriminatory act or omission was motivated by discriminatory antisemitic intent. The executive order incorporates the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance's (IHRA's) working definition of antisemitism. According to the IHRA's working definition, antisemitism is a certain perception of Jews, which may be expressed as hatred toward Jews.

This measure would require local school districts and colleges that receive federal funds to take discrimination motivated by antisemitism as seriously as they take other forms of discrimination already banned under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which covers discrimination based on race, color, or national origin in federally funded programs.

When federal agencies, school districts, and colleges review or investigate whether an action or failure to act was motivated by antisemitic intent, they would have to consider a definition of antisemitism from a December 11, 2019, executive order. That order adopts the working definition used by the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA). Under that definition, antisemitism is a certain perception of Jews, which may be expressed as hatred toward Jews.
